target_customer: People who menstruate, buying online and in retail stores
problem: Tampons and pads are uncomfortable and wasteful; menstrual discs offer up to 12 hours of wear but the market had been abandoned by incumbents.
business_model: consumer products sold DTC and through retail (Walmart, Target, CVS, Walgreens)

founders.name: Lauren Schulte Wang
founders.background_notes: Source: https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/the-flex-company. TechCrunch Aug 2016 names her as the only founder.

founders.name: Panpan Wang
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder and CFO on the YC page.

competitors.name: Softcup
competitors.what: disposable menstrual disc, acquired by Flex in 2016
competitors.traction_then: maker had planned to discontinue it

competitors.name: DivaCup
competitors.what: reusable menstrual cup named as an alternative

technical_complexity.rationale: Medical-grade silicone product design, manufacturing and regulatory clearance; patented notch and later reusable disc after 2+ years of R&D.

defensibility.rationale: Owned the disposable disc category by acquiring Softcup and holds patents, but cup makers and new discs entered.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent move found in sources; Flex bought Softcup in 2016 and Keela in 2018 and grew into 30,000 retail stores.

market_need_then: TechCrunch 2016 presents discs as a tampon alternative with the only disposable disc maker exiting; the founder ran customer sessions with women in her apartment for early research.

identity.voice_and_tone: frank and body-positive, tagline 'Love your body. Change your period.'

branding.brand_signature: the tagline 'Not a cup. Better than a tampon.'
branding.community_and_virality: Founder hosted customer groups at home; a customer, Kate Upton, led to investment from her and Justin Verlander in 2024 per Beauty Independent.

brand_strength.rationale: Distinct voice, retail presence in 30,000 stores and celebrity investor engagement, but no evidence of the name itself driving growth.

outcome_analysis: Flex bought the only disposable menstrual disc maker in 2016, raised about $1M from YC and others, then $3.6M in 2018 while acquiring Keela, and later reached 30,000 retail stores including Walmart and Target. Beauty Independent reports $20M raised before a 2024 investment from Justin Verlander and Kate Upton, and the company acquired Allbodies Health in late 2025. It is active and independent but not yet exited.
notes: Beauty Independent says $20M raised before the 2024 round, but only about $4.6M is itemized here, so rounds are missing (investors named: Halogen Ventures, Quest Venture Partners). Total funding conflicts: Fortune and LA Business Journal say $7.9M by 2018, LA Tech Watch $7.7M, CB Insights $7.62M and labels the 2018 round Series B; Dealroom gives $10M to $50M. The 2018 $3.6M round comes from Fortune and the LA Business Journal via search summaries (Fortune not opened). Founder founded year on YC page is 2015 while some articles say 2016. Executive Panpan Wang is listed only on the YC page. Competitor list uses only TechCrunch Aug 2016. First outcome search returned only Flex Ltd, an unrelated manufacturer, and found nothing for this company; no layoffs or shutdown seen in other results.
